We address the general cost-sensitive multi-label classification problem without relying on criterion-specific subroutines, thereby meeting the demands of real-world applications. We propose the condensed filter tree (CFT) algorithm, combining several tools and ideas: the label powerset approach to reduce the problem to cost-sensitive classification, tree-based algorithms for cost-sensitive classification, the proper-ordering and K-classifier tricks that exploit the structural properties of multi-label classification, and a theoretical bound for identifying the key tree nodes (paths) to train. In terms of the number of possible labels, CFT is as efficient in training and prediction as common label-wise decomposition approaches.
